title: 1C opened, but there are no customers. What happened?
goal: Find or install a lawful training platform, open your own empty infobase and explain why an empty application window is the correct first result.

prerequisites.text: Be able to open a folder and a text file in Windows.
No ready-made 1C application configuration is required.

sections.title: A familiar situation and a checkable question
paragraphs: The platform is installed and your own infobase opens, but there is no Customers menu. Is installation broken, or is this expected? Separate the program, the future application definition and particular records.

sections.title: Which program to use
paragraphs: Perform actions in the program named at the start of each step. Nexus shows the lesson and can store an optional note. Designer and 1C:Enterprise belong to installed 1C. We are studying an empty infobase; no programming or ready-made service desk is needed.
If a suitable lawful installation already works, do not reinstall it to match an image. Begin with a separate own training infobase; use no work data or somebody else’s startup entries.

sections.title: One brand, several different things
paragraphs: “Install 1C” is an incomplete specification. The platform supplies common mechanisms: windows, infobase access, module execution and data operations. A configuration describes a domain: which customers, requests and services exist, what can be saved and how results are calculated. An infobase holds a particular application instance and its data. Several infobases can use one installed platform. A shortcut label therefore does not establish that the intended infobase is open.

In our service desk, Request as a future document type belongs to the configuration. Request REQ-001 from invented customer Alpha is data. Version 8.3.27.2214 identifies the platform. Confusing these layers can make you mistake a software update for a data transfer or submit configuration sources instead of completed work. Separate the layers before making your first change.

Think of a text editor: the installed program is not the same thing as your document. Similarly, one 1C platform installation can open several independent infobases. In this course, Training service desk is the application we build ourselves, not a third-party product to download. We begin with our own empty infobase; customers and requests appear after we define their objects.

sections.title: Reason through the actions before clicking
paragraphs: The platform supplies mechanisms; records belong to the selected infobase. A shortcut name does not replace checking which location you open.
First name the window, object and expected change. An illustrative model supports reasoning; it does not mean records already exist in your infobase.

sections.title: What an application contributes
paragraphs: The platform does not inherently know what “request closed” means. The application defines that rule. Identical words in different configurations may represent different actions. Saving generally persists an object state; posting reflects a business event according to configuration rules. Posting does not automatically mean payment or completion. A1 establishes vocabulary and a model; actual catalogs and documents are introduced in later modules.

The learning model contains three requests lasting 30, 45 and 30 minutes. Their sum is 105 minutes, but this is not yet revenue, employee workload or paid labor: we have not defined those rules. A careful user checks the meaning, unit and selection behind a metric before drawing conclusions. This habit is more useful than memorizing button positions.

A beginner has two separate questions: which application window am I using, and what has already been created in my infobase? The title and launch command answer the first. Configuration and saved data answer the second. Instructions for a different accounting or payroll application need not match an empty training infobase: commands, business rules and protected objects can differ.

paragraphs: No. The platform already opens the infobase. The configuration defines the application; particular customers are entered after defining the catalog.

sections.title: A lawful training environment
paragraphs: The main free route uses the official version for learning programming supplied by 1C. If a suitable platform is already lawfully installed, first check its version and suitability for your own training infobase. Do not copy keys, licenses or third-party configurations. The conditions of the chosen distribution apply whether you launch it from a shortcut or another tool.

The training edition is for learning and has limitations. These labs do not demonstrate a multi-user deployment, password-based access protection or real business operations. Begin with a file infobase, one session and invented records. Nexus does not redistribute the platform: obtain it from its rights holder. A professional environment is considered separately when a task actually needs one.

sections.title: Landmarks while acting
paragraphs: Trace the transitions and name what changes at each step. This diagram explains; it neither creates an infobase nor operates installed 1C.

sections.title: Check another explanation
paragraphs: Open the empty application and explain why Customers is absent. Do not reinstall the platform or delete the infobase: its objects have not been created.
That is expected for an empty infobase. We will create the catalog ourselves; the installed platform does not contain your service desk records.

sections.title: Record a result that can be checked
paragraphs: Record the application name, a safe infobase alias and the full platform version separately. A configuration version does not replace a platform version. An unlabeled screenshot does not explain the operation tested. A concise protocol includes the action, expected result, observed result and limits of the conclusion.

Without an installed platform, you can study theory and classify items with the interactive diagram. This is useful preparation, but it is not 1C execution. Diagram buttons explain a model; they do not create an infobase or execute BSL. Attest a laboratory step only after observing it in the official environment.

The first observable result is deliberately concrete: your infobase appears in the startup list, Designer displays a metadata tree, and Enterprise mode opens without application sections. An empty window is normal because we have not described the application yet. Marking the lesson complete in Nexus records your self-report; it does not create a configuration or install the platform.

sections.title: Now a new independent task
paragraphs: Create another own empty training infobase with a clear name. Open it in Designer and 1C:Enterprise one at a time. In your note classify a new example: platform version, Repair document type and repair REM-017 for invented customer North. Do not define the document yet or look for it in the empty application.
Record your prediction before acting. Reveal the reference after your attempt; it explains reasoning and does not replace your own note.

steps.where: Nexus → common lab instructions; then the official 1C installer
steps.action: Expand the installation instructions in this lesson. If a suitable lawful installation is missing, obtain the official training distribution, extract the whole ZIP with Extract all and follow the 1C installer. Then find 1C:Enterprise in the Windows Start menu.
steps.why: Later actions require the real program rather than a syntax-highlighted web page.
steps.expected: The standard 1C startup list or official installed shortcut opens.

steps.action: Select Add → create a new infobase. Choose an infobase without a configuration for development. Name your entry “My training service desk”. Select a new empty directory in your own study documents for the file infobase and finish the wizard.
steps.why: A separate directory keeps experiments apart from other people’s work and business records.
steps.expected: Your new entry points to your new directory.

steps.action: Open Designer. If the tree is hidden, choose Configuration → Open configuration. Find the root and the Catalogs section. Do not change any properties yet.
steps.why: The tree describes the application rather than showing customer records.
steps.expected: Designer displays the object categories of your own empty infobase.

steps.where: Designer and the standard 1C startup list
steps.action: Close your training Designer. Select the same entry and open Enterprise mode. Inspect the empty application, close it, then reopen Designer from the same entry. Write down the three layers in your study notes.
steps.why: Switching modes neither creates catalogs nor deletes the infobase. Reopening checks which location you selected.
steps.expected: Both modes open from your own entry; missing application sections are explained by the absence of objects.
